overview:
Need to get from Marrakech to the Sahara without joining a tour? This private transfer takes you from your riad or hotel in Marrakech to your hotel or desert camp in Merzouga, at the foot of the Erg Chebbi dunes, in one long but beautiful day. Your own driver and air-conditioned vehicle, no strangers, no fixed timetable: you leave when you want and stop where you want.

AT A GLANCE
• Distance: about 560 km
• Driving time: about 7–8 hours at the wheel, 9–10 hours door to door with stops
• Start: your riad or hotel in Marrakech (or Marrakech Menara airport on request)
• Finish: your hotel in Merzouga or the meeting point of your desert camp
• Vehicle: air-conditioned car for 1–3 people, 4x4 or minivan for families and groups
• Driver: professional, English- or French-speaking, who knows the road and the stops
• Type: private, one way (the return or an onward transfer to Fes can be added)

THE ROUTE, HOUR BY HOUR
• 0h – Pick-up in Marrakech and out across the Haouz plain.
• ~2h30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass (about 2,260 m), the highest paved pass in Morocco: photo stop over the High Atlas.
• ~4h – Ouarzazate, coffee break. Ait Ben Haddou (UNESCO) is a 30-minute detour if you want it.
• ~5h30 – Skoura palm grove and the Valley of Roses at Kelaat M'Gouna.
• ~6h30 – Lunch in the Dades Valley, with its red rock formations.
• ~7h30 – Tinghir viewpoint over the palm grove; the Todra Gorge is a short detour.
• ~9h – Tinejdad, Erfoud and the first sight of the dunes.
• ~9h30–10h – Arrival in Merzouga, in time for a sunset camel ride if your camp has planned one.

PRIVATE TRANSFER, SHARED TOUR OR BUS?
• Bus: the cheapest, but it runs on a fixed timetable, often takes 11 hours or more, makes no scenic stops and leaves you at a station, not at your camp.
• Shared minibus tour: lower price, but you follow a group schedule and can't choose where or how long to stop.
• Private transfer: your own car and driver, door to door, at your pace. Split between two to four people, it is often closer to the cost of a shared tour than people expect.

GOOD TIMING
Leave Marrakech between 6:30 and 7:30. You'll reach Merzouga in the late afternoon with time to check in before sunset, which is when most desert camps start their camel rides. In winter, snow can close the Tichka pass for a few hours; your driver checks the road the evening before.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Independent travellers who have booked their own desert camp or hotel, families who want comfort and flexibility, and travellers continuing to Fes who need a reliable first leg.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you'd like the camel ride, the camp and the return included, see the [3-day Marrakech to Merzouga tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/3-days-trip-from-marrakech-to-merzouga-desert/680bc6a5aa6f43072c7700f6).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
When booking, tell us your pick-up address, the name of your hotel or camp in Merzouga, how many suitcases you have and whether you need child seats.
descriptions:
A full travel day across Morocco, from the palm groves of Marrakech over the High Atlas and along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs to the edge of the Sahara. Your driver picks you up at your riad or hotel at the time you choose (we recommend around 7:00) and sets a relaxed pace, with a stop roughly every hour and a half.

The first big moment is the climb over the Tizi n'Tichka pass, where the road winds past Berber villages and terraced fields to about 2,260 m, with wide views over the mountains. On the southern side the landscape turns dry and red. Stop for coffee in Ouarzazate, or ask your driver for the short detour to Ait Ben Haddou, the earthen ksar listed by UNESCO, for photos from across the river.

The afternoon follows the oases east: the Skoura palm grove, the rose hedges of Kelaat M'Gouna and the Dades Valley, where you can have lunch with a view of its red rock formations. After the viewpoint over the Tinghir palm grove, the road crosses the stony plain past Tinejdad and Erfoud until the dunes of Erg Chebbi appear on the horizon. Your driver takes you right to your hotel or to the meeting point where your camp's camel caravan or 4x4 is waiting.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:00 – Pick-up in Marrakech
09:30 – Tizi n'Tichka (photo stop)
11:00 – Ouarzazate (coffee; optional detour to Ait Ben Haddou)
12:30 – Skoura and the Valley of Roses
13:30 – Lunch in the Dades Valley (not included)
15:00 – Tinghir viewpoint (optional detour to the Todra Gorge)
17:00 – Drop-off in Merzouga

GOOD TO KNOW
• Optional additions (ask when booking): Ait Ben Haddou, the Dades gorge hairpins or the Todra Gorge, each adding about 45 minutes to 1.5 hours.
• Your driver can deliver you to your hotel or to the meeting point of your camp; tell us its name in advance.
• Child seats available on request.
• Keep a warm layer handy for the pass and water and snacks for the long afternoon.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, fuel, tolls, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: meals, entrance fees for optional visits, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Your driver knows good roadside restaurants: a Berber omelette near Ouarzazate, a tagine in the Dades, fresh dates near Erfoud.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: in winter, snow can close the Tichka pass for a few hours; your driver checks before leaving and adapts the timing.

ACCESSIBILITY
Comfortable seats and stops every 1.5–2 hours; tell us about any mobility needs so we choose the right vehicle.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: half of Morocco in one day, and a stress-free arrival in the Sahara.

faq.question: How long is the drive from Marrakech to Merzouga?
faq.answer: About 560 km. Driving time alone is around 7 to 8 hours, because the road crosses the High Atlas and winds through valleys. With coffee, photo and lunch stops, plan 9 to 10 hours door to door. Leaving around 7:00 gets you to Merzouga in the late afternoon.

faq.question: What route does the transfer take?
faq.answer: The classic southern route: the N9 over the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Ouarzazate, then east through Skoura, the Valley of Roses, the Dades Valley and Tinghir, then Tinejdad and Erfoud to Merzouga. It's the most scenic road to the Sahara and passes many of southern Morocco's highlights.

faq.question: Can we stop at Ait Ben Haddou or the Todra Gorge on the way?
faq.answer: Yes. Both are close to the route. Ait Ben Haddou adds about 45 minutes to an hour for a photo stop, and the Todra Gorge about the same for a short walk between the canyon walls. Tell us when booking or simply ask your driver on the day; on a private transfer you set the pace.

faq.question: Is this a private transfer?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle and driver are for your group only. You choose the pick-up time, the stops and how long you stay at each one. There's no minimum group size.

faq.question: What vehicle will we have?
faq.answer: An air-conditioned car for one to three people, and a 4x4 or a minivan for larger families and groups, with room for your luggage. Tell us how many suitcases you have, and whether you need child seats, when you book.

faq.question: Can you pick us up at Marrakech airport?
faq.answer: Yes. If you land in the morning, we can collect you at Marrakech Menara airport and drive straight to the desert, so you don't need a night in Marrakech first. Send us your flight number and we'll follow any delay.

faq.question: Will the driver take us to our desert camp?
faq.answer: Yes, to your hotel in Merzouga or to the meeting point your camp has given you, where its camels or 4x4 usually wait to take guests into the dunes. Give us the camp's name and phone number in advance so the driver can coordinate the arrival time.

faq.question: Is Merzouga the same as Erg Chebbi?
faq.answer: Almost. Merzouga is the small village at the western edge of Erg Chebbi, the great field of orange dunes that rise up to about 150 metres. Hotels sit along the edge of the dunes and most camps are among them, so people use both names for the same area.

faq.question: Why choose a private transfer rather than the bus?
faq.answer: The bus is cheaper but follows a fixed timetable, takes 11 hours or more with no scenic stops, and drops you at a station rather than your hotel or camp. A private transfer is faster, more comfortable, goes door to door and lets you see the highlights on the way. Shared between a few people, the difference in price is smaller than many expect.

faq.question: Can we book the return, or continue to Fes?
faq.answer: Yes. We drive Merzouga to Marrakech, and also Merzouga to Fes, about 7–8 hours through the Ziz Valley, Midelt and the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas. Book it together with this transfer or separately once your dates are confirmed.

faq.question: Are meals included?
faq.answer: No. Lunch and drinks are not included, so you can eat wherever you like; your driver knows good roadside restaurants, for example in Ouarzazate or the Dades Valley. Bottled water is provided in the vehicle.

faq.question: Is the road safe?
faq.answer: Yes. The road is paved all the way and well maintained. The only tricky part is the winding Tichka pass, which our drivers cross every week. In winter, snow can close the pass for a few hours; your driver checks conditions before leaving and adjusts the timing.

faq.question: When should I book?
faq.answer: As early as you can in the busy seasons, March to May and October to December, especially for larger vehicles. Outside these months, a few days' notice is usually enough. Booking early also lets us coordinate the arrival time with your desert camp.
